card.name: Cheraw (Bamboo dance)
card.tagline: Mizoram's clapping-bamboo dance of rhythm and balance
card.profile: Cheraw is the traditional bamboo dance of the Mizo people of Mizoram, considered one of the oldest Mizo dances with origins possibly dating to the 1st century AD (Wikipedia). Six to eight people, usually men, hold pairs of long bamboo staves laid across horizontal bamboos on the ground and clap them rhythmically while female dancers step intricately in and out, avoiding the closing poles; movements imitate swaying trees and flying birds. Women wear the vakiria headdress, thihna necklace, kawrchei blouse and puanchei sarong. Once a ritual for the soul of a mother who died in childbirth, it is now performed at festivals such as Chapchar Kut (Wikipedia; Amar Chitra Katha).
card.insight: On 12 March 2010 Mizoram set a Guinness World Record for the largest bamboo dance when 10,736 people performed Cheraw in unison - 2,518 at the Assam Rifles Ground and 8,218 along the streets of Aizawl (Guinness World Records).

observation.setting: An outdoor courtyard with a concrete floor, decorated with flower arrangements, with a seated audience watching from the edges.
observation.dancers: A large group of mixed young men and women, performing in separate roles (some sitting and tapping bamboo poles, others dancing).
observation.formation_and_space: Multiple parallel lines of dancers stepping between long, parallel bamboo poles laid on the ground, which are rhythmically tapped by kneeling participants.
observation.posture: Upright torso for standing dancers with a slight bounce in the knees; kneeling pole-tappers are crouched down close to the ground.
observation.footwork: Stepping and hopping in and out of the gaps between the bamboo poles on the beat, keeping time with the tapping of the bamboo.
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held loosely at the sides or resting on hips for dancers; pole-tappers use their hands to hold and strike the bamboo poles together.
observation.hips_and_torso: Minimal torso movement, mainly upright and steady while the legs and feet execute the stepping patterns.
observation.partnering: None; individual steps executed in synchronization alongside others in lines.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Low level for pole-tappers crouching on the ground; standing level for dancers with light hopping and stepping.
observation.costume_and_props: Dancers wear traditional-style patterned skirts, white shirts with striped borders, and feathered headbands; pole-tappers wear plaid shirts and dark shorts. Props consist of long bamboo poles.
observation.cannot_infer: Exact foot placement inside the bamboo grid and subtle ankle work are partially obscured by long skirts and camera distance.

signature_moments.what: Dancers step rapidly in unison between the clapping bamboo poles, keeping time with the percussive rhythm.
